title: Lecture 4 · Enzymes and their catalytic roles

blocks.html:
What to know

  • Enzymes lower activation energy. They stabilize the transition state; they do not change the overall free-energy change or the equilibrium position.
  • The active site is a shaped pocket. Substrates bind through specific weak interactions. Induced fit means the enzyme changes shape slightly on binding.
  • Kinetics describe capacity and affinity. Vmax reflects enzyme amount and turnover; Km is the substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity and is an inverse measure of apparent affinity.
  • Inhibition can be competitive or non-competitive. A competitive inhibitor binds the active site and raises apparent Km; a non-competitive inhibitor binds elsewhere and lowers Vmax.
  • Regulation matches demand. Allosteric effectors, covalent modification (for example phosphorylation), and enzyme synthesis/degradation change flux through a pathway.

Check

check.question: A drug binds the active site of an enzyme and can be overcome by more substrate. What kind of inhibition is it?
check.explanation: Competitive inhibitors compete with substrate for the active site, so raising substrate concentration restores velocity.
